                    ### Question
                    A 57-year-old woman is admitted to the intensive care unit for management of shock. Her pulse is feeble and blood pressure is 86/45 mm Hg. The patient undergoes pulmonary artery catheterization which shows an elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure and increased systemic vascular resistance. Which of the following additional findings is most likely in this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Cold skin due to loss of intravascular fluid volume
opb. Bradycardia due to neurologic dysfunction
opc. Bronchospasm due to excessive histamine release
opd. Mottled skin due to release of endotoxins
ope. Confusion due to decreased stroke volume

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In a patient with shock, an elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure and increased systemic vascular resistance are indicative of fluid overload rather than loss of intravascular fluid volume leading to cold skin. Mottled skin due to release of endotoxins is a more likely finding in shock. Confusion due to decreased stroke volume is a plausible consequence of shock, while bradycardia due to neurologic dysfunction and bronchospasm due to excessive histamine release are less likely in this context.
